content.title: Re-watch the full Chicago River dyeing as St. Patrick's Day celebrations kick off
content.text: The annual tradition of dyeing the river green dates back to 1961. NBC Universal, Inc. As the 2026 river dye celebration wraps up, take another look at the moment the Chicago River transformed into its iconic bright green color. One of the Windy City's most famous traditions took place Saturday as thousands flocked to the downtown area to watch the Chicago River turn bright green. The festive fun kicked off at 10 a.m. on Saturday, with boatloads of members of the Chicago Plumbers Local 130 union spraying a dye concoction into the waters of the Chicago River to celebrate the St. Patrick's Day holiday. The annual tradition of dyeing the river green dates back to 1961 when Stephen Bailey, the business manager of the Chicago Plumbers Local 130 union, came up with the idea after seeing a plumber whose overalls had been dyed a bright green by a dye that was used to detect leaks in the sewer system along the Chicago River. Though the dye turns the water bright emerald, it looks orange until it hits the surface of the river. Shortly after the river dyeing concluded, a pair of professional jet ski riders put on a thrilling high-speed performance on the emerald waters. Looking to keep the festive fun going? Check out a miniature version of the shamrock-colored river on display through the end of March over in Schaumburg at the LEGOLAND Discovery Center Chicago in The Streets of Woodfield shopping center, located at 601 N. Martingale Rd. Local There are also several St. Patrick's Day events happening throughout the city on Sunday and Tuesday. A look at the lineup of events across the area can be found here.
